observations.claim: No step indicator anywhere in the funnel — the user has no idea this is step 1 of 4; the body Column goes straight from title to chips (SlotPickerScreen.kt:110-137).
Time windows are rendered as raw API strings (e.g. '09:00-11:00') with no localisation, no AM/PM, and no Devanagari numerals.

Screen bypasses the design system: uses raw Material3 Button (:144) and raw Card (:297) rather than HsPrimaryButton / HsSectionCard used by every other funnel screen, so the primary CTA here is visually different from the CTA on Address and Summary.

DATE_DISPLAY is a file-level DateTimeFormatter created without a Locale, so the date chips are formatted with the JVM default locale captured at class load and will not follow an in-app en/hi locale switch.
Selecting a slot produces no visual confirmation beyond the default FilterChip checkmark, and the sticky CTA gives no summary of what was chosen.
Section bucketing is derived by string-parsing the hour out of the window label, so a malformed window silently sorts into 'Morning'.

observations.claim: Two different address-entry screens exist behind a feature flag with different visual languages (this one is a form + flat preview box; the other is a full-bleed map), so the funnel's step 2 is visually inconsistent depending on flag state.

observations.claim: AddressPickerUiState.Error is emitted by the ViewModel but has no UI branch; the state machine silently falls into the default CTA branch, leaving the user with a disabled button and zero explanation.
When reverse geocoding fails after a pin drag, the confirmed address shown to the user is the literal string 'Lat 26.79, Lng 82.19' — raw coordinates presented as an address, untranslated.
No 'use my current location' control exists on the Places variant even though the legacy AddressScreen has one — a rural user with a low-literacy profile must type a query or drag a pin.
The 'Notify me' refusal CTA reuses onConfirm, so a refused user and a confirming user hit the same ViewModel entry point; the button label promises a subscription the screen does not visibly perform.
Marker is only rendered once coordinates exist, so on first open the user sees a bare map of Ayodhya with no pin and no instruction of what to do.
Two shadow elevations (4.dp search, 8.dp predictions and bottom bar) are hand-typed rather than taken from HomeservicesElevation.

surfaces.density: Cramped decision cards: name+description+price+two buttons packed into one HsSectionCard with 16.dp internal padding (HsComponents.kt:119) and no separation between the info Row and the button Row (PriceApprovalScreen.kt:138 → :149 have no Spacer at all), so the buttons touch the description.

observations.claim: Two different currency renderings appear within ~45 lines of each other — 'Rs 499' for each add-on and '₹499.00' for the total.
The screen has no back/close affordance at all: the TopAppBar declares only a title, so a user who does not want to decide right now cannot leave except via the system back gesture.

Approve and Decline are given identical prominence and identical weight — a filled HsPrimaryButton and an outlined HsSecondaryButton side by side — but they also render at different heights because HsPrimaryButton is space16 (64.dp) and HsSecondaryButton is space12 (48.dp), so the two halves of the decision row are visibly mismatched.

Selection state is communicated only by swapping the button label text ('Approve'→'Approved'); there is no colour, fill, icon or elevation change, so a glanceable read of which add-ons were approved is impossible.
The error state renders a raw exception inside 'Error: %s' with no retry and no exit.
An empty add-on list produces an enabled Confirm button over an empty list and a zero total.
Decisions are held in a composition-local mutableStateMapOf keyed on bookingId rather than in the ViewModel, so process death loses every decision the user made.

observations.claim: There is no moment of delight: the success affordance is a static Icons.Filled.CheckCircle inside a tinted Surface, with zero animation, zero motion tokens, no haptic and no sound — the whole file contains no animate*/AnimatedVisibility call.
The confirmation recaps nothing the user bought — no service name, no date/time slot, no address, no amount payable in cash. The only booking-specific datum on the screen is the raw booking ID.

The three timeline steps all render with an identical primary-coloured square dot because HsTimelineStep hard-codes colorScheme.primary, so 'done', 'in progress' and 'not started' are visually indistinguishable.
The Column is not scrollable, so on a small screen with Hindi text plus the TrustDossierCard the two stacked CTAs can be pushed out of reach.
The two stacked CTAs have mismatched heights (56.dp over 52.dp) and neither matches the design-system button token.
TrustDossierCard is wired but the nav destination never passes technicianId (MainGraph.kt:378-383 supplies only bookingId and appliedCredit), so in production the card never renders on this screen.

surfaces.density: Inconsistent: 16.dp padding around the header and progress card but 3.dp vertical padding between timeline rows (LiveTrackingScreen.kt:344), so the status timeline is visually cramped inside an otherwise airy layout. The 300.dp map and the 300.dp placeholder dominate the fold, pushing the progress card below it.

observations.claim: The status chip label — the primary piece of information on the tracking screen — is hard-coded English via statusLabel(), in an app whose target market is Hindi-speaking Ayodhya.
LiveTrackingUiState has no Error variant, so any failure leaves the user on an indefinite bare centred spinner with no retry and no message.
The technician's photo is fetched and carried into UI state but never displayed — the trust-critical avatar is missing from a screen about a stranger entering your home.
Both AssistChips are declared with onClick = {} — they look and behave like interactive controls (ripple, focus, TalkBack 'button') but do nothing.
liveCapturedAt is populated in state but no 'last updated' or staleness indicator is rendered, so a frozen live location is indistinguishable from a stationary technician.
The map camera position is set once in rememberCameraPositionState and never re-centred as the marker moves, so the technician can drift out of the visible viewport.
The SOS control only exists while status is InProgress; before arrival (EnRoute/Reached) there is no safety affordance at all.
The technician name is rendered as a plain Text in headlineSmall rather than HsScreenTitle, so it carries no heading semantics for TalkBack navigation.
